title: A stiffer spring oscillator
hook: Change spring stiffness and predict oscillation period.
misconception: oscillation period doubles when spring stiffness doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply T = 2π√(m/k) to compare oscillation period when spring stiffness changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ideal horizontal spring with fixed attached mass, T = 2π√(m/k). When spring stiffness doubles, oscillation period becomes 1/√2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model T = 2π√(m/k); scaling exponent -0.5. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ideal horizontal spring with fixed attached mass, with a nonzero initial result. If spring stiffness triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on oscillation period?
recall.why: Apply T = 2π√(m/k) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/√3.
